subject: c-fo-act
title: C.FO.ACT.------T.C.IMP.
description: Diagram in MID-W-12, on the page where Braxton describes the AACM's free music school program — 'in 1967, the Association for the Advancement of Creative Musicians addressed itself to one of the most important problems facing the black community' — and the structural commitment to community engagement. C-FO-ACT (composite focused activism) is crossed with T-C-IMP (time continuum implications). EXP-DYM (expansion dynamics) → T-C-IMP; RT-ALGN (reality alignment) → T-C-IMP and RT-ALGN → C-FO-ACT (the subject); MT-INFO (music information) → T-C-IMP. T-C-IMP → DYM-F (dynamic functionalism) → PHY-U-P (physical universe particular) and T-C-IMP → CULT-INFO-DY (culture information dynamics) ← POL-DYM (political dynamics) ← C-CONT (composite continuance). RT-ALGN has a *dashed* edge to INFO-INTR (information interpretation). Structural argument: composite focused activism is fed by reality alignment (and reality alignment also feeds time-continuum implications directly), with the time-continuum implications hub being further over-fed by expansion dynamics and music information. Dynamic functionalism produces physical universe particular as terminal. Culture information dynamics is fed by both time-continuum implications and political dynamics (which is itself fed by composite continuance). The dashed edge from reality alignment to information interpretation is critical: it marks that reality alignment's role in shaping interpretation is *conditional* — meaning the AACM's music school programs do not automatically produce the reframing of black creativity's interpretation; that reframing is conditional on the alignment work actually penetrating the interpretive layer. The diagram thus diagrams both the strength and the precarity of the AACM's community engagement: the structural conditions are in place, but the interpretation-shifting effect is not guaranteed.
